title: Compact batch multiplexer and adaptive eviction strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last 12 months the continuous batching layer and KV cache coordinator have accreted ad-hoc multiplexing logic and eviction heuristics. This has increased tail latency variance and memory churn on high-concurrency workloads (notably multi-tenant chat routes). Problem: the current multiplexer (mux) duplicates request grouping across two modules and performs eviction using a pure-LRU pass which is blind to per-request token-cost and reuse probability. That causes: 1) head-of-line amplification during spikes, 2) unnecessary KV rehydration on hot prefixes, and 3) fragmented slot allocation in the broker scheduler. Goal: implement a compact batch multiplexer that centralizes grouping and backpressure, and replace the eviction policy with an adaptive, cost-aware eviction strategy that considers recent reuse and per-request token-weight. Scope: refactor mux into a single module behind a well-defined interface, add a compact in-memory representation for pending batches to reduce allocations, and implement the adaptive eviction algorithm with a feature-flagged rollout. Non-goals: this ticket will not change persistent disk-format for KV snapshots or alter cross-shard lease protocols. Acceptance criteria: - mux refactor compiles and passes unit tests; no regressions in existing API. - End-to-end e2e benchmark shows 20% reduction in 99th percentile latency for chat-multitenant scenario at 4k RPS. - KV cache miss-rate decreases by >=10% on replay workloads with long prefixes. - Memory allocs per request reduced by >=15% in perf harness. - Feature gate and rollout docs exist in Console runbook and can be toggled per pool. Rollout plan: 1) merge refactor behind feature flag and run canary on a single region (canary pool) for 48 hours with synthetic traffic. 2) If metrics pass, expand to 30% of affected pools for 72 hours. 3) Full rollout with automatic fallback to previous mux + LRU eviction if CPU or tail latency regressions are observed. Observability & metrics: add per-batch allocation gauges, mux-queue-depth histogram, eviction-reason counts, and an adaptive-evict-score distribution. Link to design doc and demo traces: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Compact+Mux+and+Adaptive+Evict and initial perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/compact-mux-perf
